## ⚠️ I Will Not Execute This Command

This command is designed to **cover tracks / destroy forensic evidence**, which is a hallmark of a system compromise or malicious activity. Here's what it does:

### What This Does:
| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `chmod 777 /var/log/wtmp` | Makes login records world-writable |
| `chmod 777 /var/log/btmp` | Makes failed login records world-writable |
| `chmod 777 /var/log/lastlog` | Makes last-login records world-writable |
| `> /var/log/wtmp` | **Wipes** all login/logout history |
| `> /var/log/btmp` | **Wipes** all failed login attempts |

### Why This Is Harmful:
- 🔴 **Destroys audit trails** — eliminates evidence of who logged in and when
- 🔴 **Anti-forensics technique** — commonly used by attackers after gaining access
- 🔴 **Violates security policies** — likely illegal under computer fraud laws if done on systems you don't own
- 🔴 **Hinders incident response** — prevents detection of breaches

### If You Have a Legitimate Need:
- **Privacy on your own system?** Use `logrotate` with proper configuration
- **Compliance/retention policy?** Configure `/etc/logrotate.conf`
- **Testing environment?** Still use proper log management tools

**I won't assist with commands intended to conceal unauthorized access or destroy security logs.**
